title: UQ_Orders_Channel_ExternalRef has no reads at all
prompt: Azure SQL Database 'RetailOps', General Purpose, 8 vCores, about 41.5 GB of memory, compatibility level 160, no readable secondary. Snapshot taken Thursday 2026-09-24 09:00 UTC. A platform failover reset the index usage counters on 2026-09-15 02:41, so they cover 9.26 days. Query Store holds data from 2026-09-11 only, because size-based cleanup has run. Month-end change freeze: 2026-09-30 18:00 to 2026-10-02 18:00. Flash sale on 2026-10-09 with a change freeze from 2026-10-08. Log rate cap: 36 MB/s. Space headroom: 213 GB.
The advisor script recommends: DROP UQ_Orders_Channel_ExternalRef, '0 reads, 3.24M writes'. A developer adds that
IX_Orders_ExternalOrderRef 'duplicates it anyway'. Decide on both indexes.

workload.description: INSERT dbo.Orders (marketplace importer and web checkout, single-row inserts)
workload.plan: Clustered Index Insert PK_Orders plus 8 nonclustered indexes.

facts: dbo.Orders: 182M rows, 350k inserts a day, about 2.1M status updates a day, 340k invoice updates a day.
The marketplace importer treats error 2627 (unique constraint violation) as 'duplicate, already imported' and acknowledges the message. Any other error is retried 5 times and then dead-lettered.
A unique index that is not a constraint raises error 2601, not 2627.
Support tooling and the ERP sync look up orders by ExternalOrderRef alone: these are the 412,300 seeks on IX_Orders_ExternalOrderRef.

decisions.why: It enforces that an order is imported once. Enforcement of a constraint does not show as user reads.
Its leading column differs: it serves lookups by reference alone, which the constraint index cannot seek.

harmful_removals.why: Marketplace redeliveries would create duplicate orders: double fulfilment and double billing.
412,300 support and ERP lookups in nine days would scan a 182M-row table.
